provenance.citation: Katsounaros I., Electrochemical reduction of nitrate on tin cathode: removal of nitrate from the ion exchange regenerant solution, PhD thesis (in Greek), Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (2009)
provenance.file: thesis page image via the archive's online reader, 300 dpi; not committed
provenance.notes: Terms: National Archive of PhD Theses (didaktorika.gr, run by EKT). Its terms of use allow deposited theses to be used online for educational, scientific, statistical and research purposes when there is no direct or indirect financial benefit, require any publication based on a thesis to cite its author, and allow linking to the site's content but not reproducing it; the item page states that all items in the archive are protected by copyright. The page image was viewed through the archive's online reader without an account and is not stored in the repo. Whether NernstWork's use meets the no-financial-benefit condition is the repository owner's decision. Caption: time course of (filled square) NO3-, (open circle) NO2-, (filled down-triangle) N2, (open triangle) NH3, (star) N2O during electrolysis on Sn at -2.4 V vs Ag/AgCl, 2 M NaCl + 0.05 M NaNO3. Analytics (thesis ch. 5): NO3- and NO2- by ion chromatography, NH3 by OPA fluorescence, H2/N2/N2O by on-line GC-TCD with instantaneous readings integrated over time. Text facts on the page: NO3- 3.2 mM at 90 min (digitized 3.23); NO2- shows a small maximum at 15 min quoted as 1.15 mM, but the plotted circle sits at 0.60 mM (its full outline is visible, 0.55-0.65 mM allowing for marker overlap), so text and figure disagree by about a factor 2 and the digitized value follows the figure; selectivities as in n_basis_note; experimental error about 10 %. Diag 6.7 (same electrolyte, endpoint after 1 h vs potential) shows at -2.4 V NO3- 4.5, NH3 13.4, N2 16.5 mM, which lies between the 60 and 90 min points here, so the two diagrams are probably not the same run.
provenance.extraction: Raster digitization of the thesis page image (reader page 111, 300 dpi, 2481x3509 px) by an agent script (OpenCV), not WebPlotDigitizer; the wpd_datasets.csv here is written in the WebPlotDigitizer unified layout. Axes calibrated linearly from located tick-mark centres: x from 0 min (px 678.0) to 90 min (px 1851.0), all seven major ticks evenly spaced to within 1 px; y from 0 mM (px 1556.0) to 50 mM (px 705.5), all eleven ticks evenly spaced to within 1 px (17.01 px/mM, so 1 px = 0.06 mM). Filled squares (NO3-), filled down-triangles (N2) and open up-triangles (NH3) were located by normalized cross-correlation with templates cut from the clean 90 min markers, searched within +-6 px of each sampling-time tick; open stars (N2O) the same way. Marker anchor = geometric centre: bounding-box centre for the square, area centroid (circumcentre) for the triangles, circumcentre (top + h/1.809) for the five-pointed star; the connecting lines enter the triangles at the centroid, not the box centre. Open circles (NO2-) were located by a ring fit (radius 8.5-9 px, arc samples hidden by the x-axis line excluded), because at 15 and 30 min the circle encloses or touches the N2O star. Occluded markers matched with lower confidence: NH3 at 15 min (under the N2 triangle tip) and 45 min (over the NO3- square), N2O at 15 min (inside the NO2- circle), NO2- at 30 min. At t = 0 the product markers are drawn on top of each other at the origin and are entered as 0; NO3- at t = 0 (49.68, square clipped by the frame) is pinned to 50 mM by the converter. The NO3- error bars (caps measured at 15-60 min: +-10 % of the value; at 75-90 min hidden behind the marker) were not carried as sigma because the thesis does not say whether they are one standard deviation. The NO3- curve is the author's exponential fit and was not digitized. Inverse-calibration overlay checked by eye on the page crop (scratch, not committed). Converted with scripts/digitized_to_dataset.py.

conditions.catalyst: Sn foil (2 cm2 geometric), polished with 1200 grit before each run
conditions.stirring: He sparge 12 mL/min through the catholyte (carries gases to the on-line GC); no stirrer stated
conditions.notes: Teflon cell with Nafion 117 (H+ form) separator, 10 mL in each compartment (12 mL compartments), platinized Pt anode (6 cm2) 2 cm from the cathode, Luggin capillary to the reference. Experiments at ambient temperature (not given numerically). Unbuffered chloride electrolyte; initial and final pH not stated for this run. Not converted to RHE.

quality.n_basis_note: N2 and N2O are plotted as molecules (mM N2, mM N2O) and converted x2 to N atoms. Established from the thesis text on the same page: final selectivities NH3 28.6 %, N2 70.7 %, N2O 6 % at 90 min with NO3- 3.2 mM (46.8 mM converted). Digitized 90 min values give NH3 13.34/46.77 = 28.5 %, N2 2 x 16.59/46.77 = 70.9 %, N2O 2 x 1.41/46.77 = 6.0 %; per-N-atom plotting would give 35 % and 3 %. Closure with the x2 factor: 0.99 (15 min), 1.09, 1.10, 1.08, 1.05, 1.05 (90 min); the text attributes the 105 % selectivity sum to an experimental error of about 10 %. Without the x2 factor closure at 90 min would be 0.69.
